subject: Proposed DPA addendum — block model updates, log access & onshore routing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam O'Connor <sam.oconnor@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 10:15:00 +0000
Subject: Proposed DPA addendum — block model updates, log access & onshore routing

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for the call this morning — glad we made progress on the integration plan. As requested, attaching a short list of specific asks HealthBridge wants captured in the DPA addendum so your legal team can review and push back as needed. The main asks are:

- A binding commitment that data sent to Redwood for inference will not be used to update, fine-tune, or otherwise train any model (explicit "no model updates / no training" language).
- Onshore routing requirement for traffic from HealthBridge production tenants: US-only residency for inference processing and KV/cache persistence.
- Read-only access to anonymized request/response logs for audits (exportable for 90 days) — or a mechanism to deliver audit artifacts to HealthBridge security.
- Clarification on telemetry: which low-level metrics we retain and for how long (request ids, latency, model name) vs full prompt/response retention.

Two quick asks for next steps: could you confirm whether your side can accept pseudonymized logs rather than full prompt dumps, and whether HealthBridge has KMS requirements for keys at rest? I copied Monica (legal) and Jonas (infra/ML) to help pin technical and contractual details.

Attaching our proposed addendum draft; please review and let me know availability for a quick redline call tomorrow.

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_Draft_v2.pdf (draft addendum), SLA_Table.xlsx (impact on latency/availability targets)

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0137

From: Sam O'Connor <sam.oconnor@healthbridge.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@healthbridge.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 12:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA addendum — block model updates, log access & onshore routing

Ben — appreciate the summary and attachments. A couple of immediate clarifications from our side: 

1) "No training" language: Our legal team typically asks for the commitment to be scoped to "no incorporation into model training or continuous learning pipelines without explicit prior written consent." Can you confirm if Redwood can accept that scope, and whether it includes internal research experiments?

2) Logs: HealthBridge security prefers receipt of audit artifacts rather than ongoing log access. Would Redwood be willing to provide a weekly export of pseudonymized request/response records (fields: request_id, timestamp, model_id, prompt_hash, response_hash, latency_ms) for a 90-day rolling window? Full prompt text is a no-go for our internal auditors.

3) KMS: We require proof that customer keys are available for encryption-at-rest; do you support external KMS (BYOK) or a key-wrapping option?

I forwarded the draft to our legal team (see attached comments). We can do a call Thu 14:00 ET if that works.

Attachments: HealthBridge_DPA_comments.pdf (redline + comments)

Thanks,
Sam O'Connor
Head of Security & Privacy | HealthBridge
sam.oconnor@healthbridge.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam O'Connor <sam.oconnor@healthbridge.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA addendum — block model updates, log access & onshore routing

Sam, Ben — thanks for the detailed notes. I reviewed HealthBridge's comments and sketched a minimal redline that should be acceptable to both sides. High level: 

- "No incorporation into model training" clause: propose the following language for the addendum: 
  "Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, update, or improve any of Provider's production models or derivations thereof that are used to serve third-party customers, except with Customer's prior written consent. Provider may use aggregated, irreversible telemetry that does not include prompt or response plaintext for service improvement and debugging purposes."

- Logs/export: Redwood can provide a weekly export of pseudonymized audit artifacts (request_id, timestamp, model_id, prompt_hash, response_hash, token_count, latency_ms) via a secure S3 endpoint that HealthBridge controls. Retention configurable up to 90 days.

- KMS: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS with key-wrapping; if HealthBridge requires on-prem HSM we will need to evaluate scope under Redwood Private (separate commercial term).

Impact on SLA: Jonas — see SLA_Table.xlsx (attached). The main operational impact of strict onshore-only routing is increased tail latency for cross-region failover and additional throughput capacity if caching is disabled. I recommend we list a fallback clause that permits transient routing to a geographically proximate region for up to 1 hour for emergency failover, with notification. 

I've attached DPA_Addendum_Draft_v2.pdf with redline highlights and a short cover note. Ben — if you and Sam can confirm the export fields and the KMS approach, I will prepare a final redline for signature.

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_Draft_v2.pdf

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam O'Connor <sam.oconnor@healthbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 09:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA addendum — block model updates, log access & onshore routing

Thanks — quick technical perspective and a few asks to include in the DPA so the ops/infra teams have clear handoffs: 

> "Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, update, or improve any of Provider's production models..."

We should tighten to make clear exceptions for: 
- synthetic/aggregated telemetry (non-reversible hashes) used strictly for capacity planning and anonymized metrics; 
- internal research proofs-of-concept that do not use identifiable Customer Data and are run in isolated research sandboxes (with separate procurement approvals).

Operational considerations: 
- If HealthBridge requires onshore-only processing and persistent KV cache residency in US, we need a pinned routing policy that guarantees a US cluster and an SLA note on warm-up delays for cold cache and prefix caching impact. That will affect the latency numbers in SLA_Table.xlsx and potentially require a reserved capacity commitment for predictable tail latency.
- For the weekly pseudonymized exports: we must agree on the hashing algorithm and salt management (we recommend HMAC-SHA256 with HealthBridge-provided salt stored in their KMS). Otherwise cross-checking will be impossible.

Suggested additions to the addendum (technical appendix):
- Hashing algorithm & salt control
- Export format (Parquet/CSV), encryption-at-rest & in-flight, and delivery window (within 48h of request)
- Emergency failover window and notification procedure (1 hour max, see Monica's fallback suggestion)

Happy to sync on a 30-minute call to finalize the appendix and confirm whether this triggers Dedicated/Private offering conversations.

Jonas Weber
Director, Serving & Inference Systems | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
